body.title: Specify federative points and the voting procedure
body.body:
## What is delivered
A specification of how federative points are earned, held and counted, and how a decision of the federation is actually taken.

Cover at least: what counts as delivered work; who confirms it; whether points decay; how points map to voting weight; what can be voted on; quorum; and how a resource request is evaluated against the rule that support is a last resort.

## Why it is needed
The README states that DAOs accumulate federative points and voting power over federation resources and decisions. None of the mechanism behind that sentence is published — neither the contract, nor the point mechanics, nor the voting procedure.

For a federation whose whole premise is cooperation without an owner, this is the gap that matters most. Drayker has substantial unpublished work on its economic and resource model; this function is largely about consolidating it into something reviewable.

## Where to start
The published rules are the constraints: the initial DAO is funded by grants and side projects; support requests only where there is no alternative; resource efficiency matters; main projects are the priority. Any design has to keep those true.
## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/#org/fn

body.title: Run the first assembly, against work that already happened
body.body:
## What is delivered
One completed assembly cycle in `federation/assemblies/`, run end to end against a delivery that has already happened — not a hypothetical one.

Open the cycle as an issue, claim the delivery, draft the report from [the template](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/federation/assemblies/TEMPLATE.md), hold the seven-day window, record the tally, merge. The procedure is [DAF-001 §4](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-001-phase-0-github-federation.md#4-the-cycle).

The specification of the DAF federation itself is a candidate: it was declared in a public issue, its result is inspectable, and it closed.

## Why it is needed
The rules are written and nothing has ever been run through them. Quorum at 30% of active points, one point per function, a bonus per function on module completion — these are starting values that no use has validated. The first assembly is the cheapest possible way to find out which of them are wrong, and it costs nothing but the time to hold it.

Running it against real work also settles the awkward first question honestly: the founding steward holds a majority by construction, because the steward did the work. Better to have that visible in a real ledger than described in a document.

## Where to start
[DAF-000 §3.1](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-000-federation-constitution.md#31-what-counts-as-delivered-work) for what counts as delivered, [DAF-001 §4](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-001-phase-0-github-federation.md#4-the-cycle) for the cycle, and the three templates in `federation/`.

Expect the templates to be wrong somewhere. The last section of the assembly report exists for exactly that — write down what the rules cost to operate, so the next revision argues with evidence.

body.title: Design the ICP migration for Phase 1, against the conditions that would force it
body.body:
## What is delivered
A proposal in `dafp/` for moving the federation onto ICP: what it would run, what it costs, what it carries across, and which condition triggers the move.

## Why it is needed
ICP is the stated direction — the reason being reputation and resource management that a repository cannot carry. [DAF-001 §7](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-001-phase-0-github-federation.md#7-when-phase-0-stops-being-enough) records that direction and deliberately separates it from the trigger: naming where the work goes is not the same as deciding when it goes there.

That separation is the whole point of this function. Three previous attempts picked a platform first — Aragon on Ethereum, then DAOhaus on Optimism, then canisters on ICP — and each was abandoned before deployment. The reason was never the design. It was that a deployment demands funding, tokenomics and an audience before the federation has recorded a single decision. The direction was right more than once; the order was wrong every time.

## Where to start
[DAF-001 §6](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-001-phase-0-github-federation.md#6-what-phase-0-does-not-give-you) is the requirements list, already written: no censorship resistance, no cryptographic guarantee, no sybil resistance beyond judgment, no anonymity, no custody. A useful proposal says which of those ICP actually fixes, and at what running cost per year.

Three things worth being concrete about:

- **Migration of the record.** The history in `federation/` has to survive the move with its attributions intact. A design that starts everyone at zero throws away the only thing Phase 0 produces.
- **Anonymity.** The hardest of the conditions and the least explored — the earlier drafts describe contributors who cannot participate publicly, and no phase has an answer for them. Treating it seriously is worth more than a fast recommendation.
- **What stays out.** The transferable instrument is out of scope by [DAF-000 §6.1](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-000-federation-constitution.md#61-what-is-not-in-scope-here). A substrate that can hold one does not by itself settle whether it should.

An answer that is only a platform comparison repeats the mistake this function exists to avoid.

body.title: Bring the Português README up to date
body.body:
## What is delivered
`README.PT.md` carrying the same content as the English `README.md`, including the sections added when the specification was published.

## Why it is needed
The Portuguese README is four paragraphs describing how a unit joins and how resources work. The English one now also says what the federation is for, where the specification lives, what the record in `federation/` holds, and — importantly — what is and is not running.

That last part is what makes this more than tidiness: a reader arriving in Portuguese currently gets no warning that nothing is operational yet. The gap between the two files is the gap between an invitation and an honest one.

## Where to start
`README.md` is the source. Keep the link to the English version at the top and the note about which one is ahead.

Terms that should not be invented fresh — federative points, function, module, unit, assembly — appear across `dafp/`. Consistency with those matters more than elegance, because the same words carry the mechanics.

Translating [DAF-000](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-000-federation-constitution.md) and [DAF-001](https://github.com/draykerdk/daf/blob/master/dafp/daf-001-phase-0-github-federation.md) is a much larger job and is not part of this function. If you want it, open a separate one.

body.title: Harden the DAF site contract and clarify community scope
body.body:
## Summary

- keep the DAF interface and common record in English and remove the stale Portuguese README
- explicitly allow units organized around a language, region or nationality, without changing points or voting weight
- replace critical generic click controls with semantic links/buttons and make remaining controls keyboard accessible
- describe the pre-assembly state accurately
- validate snapshot schema and cover empty, malformed and offline states
- clarify that the repository is the record and the Pages artifact is only its reading surface

## Validation

- 42 DAF contract checks
- syntax and whitespace checks
- responsive QA at 390x844, tablet and desktop
- no overflow, broken images, console errors or unnamed buttons
- network-failure tests send no external action

body.body:
Alignment pass across the `draykerdk` organization, on the branch `alinhamento/2026-09` in every affected repository.

## Changes

- docs: unify footer
- docs: remove book citations

## Across the organization

- Governance corrected: PAP is Projects & Applications, DFMP is the DFM proposal process, the founding account is `Hyadhuad`, and the governance horizon runs from the founding Embassy through the DAF into PAP.
- The veto chain specified in UID: signed, hash-linked vetoes that carry their real grounds even when anonymous; vetoes weighed by grounds, not counted; one veto with grounds beyond the decision's scope can lead to an adjustment after advanced triage.
- Direction states 2033 as the objective, measured by what works rather than by the date.
- Intelligence is a partner, never the master.
- English is the canonical documentation language.
- Documentation states its own claims and does not cite outside books as authority.

Documentation only. Nothing here claims an implemented system.

Supersedes #11, closed when the branch was renamed.

body.title: Units of account instead of a token economy
body.body_html:
Aligns this repository with the decisions of October 2026:

  • member councils formed for each question instead of an independent judicial panel chosen by lot;
  • no forks or open-code claims for Dk: auditable through Dknowledge and DFM by permission level, with divergence tested in parallel;
  • Dk Global decides only inside the space the constitution gives it, open to representation, proposals and justified vetoes;
  • units of account instead of a token economy.

body.body:
- README and DAF-000 define DAF as an autonomous, distributed federation of autonomous units: the groups and organizations of people working on different questions and projects in Drayker.
- DAF-000 keeps a DAO as one possible kind of unit, but no longer as the default form.
- Component contract: "An operating DAO federation" → "An operating federation of autonomous units".

Founder decision (06/10/2026): DAF "é uma federação autônoma e distribuída de unidades autônomas, que são esses grupos e organizações de pessoas trabalhando em diferentes questões e projetos na Drayker", and a DAO "pode ser esse tipo de grupo… mas deixa de ser central ou o padrão".

body.title: Clarify federation charter scope, councils and DAF definition
body.body:
## What changed

- DAF-000 5.1 and site: federation votes change this document and the documents it governs, never the members' constitution or the kernel.
- DAF-000 and site: councils are formed for each question and composed by Dknowledge. Their authority over a federation vote is not specified.
- Site hero: DAF is an autonomous federation of autonomous units and a basic and primitive form of PAP implemented now.
- Footer: Drayker is non-profit.

## Founder

> "As mudanças na constituição sempre devem partir de um projeto super bem informado e validado feito em conjunto com o Dk global em cooperação com praticamente todos os membros de maior nível."

> "O Dk global deve apresentar uma alternativa ou uma aprovação da proposta, mas mudanças na constituição devem estar de acordo com o kernel, se não tiverem ele barra até que o kernel mude."

> "Isso apenas para constituição, certo? que já está ganhando destaque mais que suficiente, no resto o Dk global decide e executa autonomamente."

> "Com os membros podendo fazer o veto bem justificado."

> "Ela não é definível, a única definição que cabe é de super sistema."
